CX3CR1/CX3CL1 axis plays a key role in the pathogenesis and progression of emphysematous changes in the lung.

CX3CL1 is up-regulated during cigarette smoke-induced lung disease and this up-regulation is accompanied by the influx and retention of CX3CR+ immune cells in the lungs.
the CX3CL-CX3CR1 axis is a novel target for the treatment and prevention of emphysematic lung disease.

the chemokine receptor CX3CR1 has an important role in the recruitment and accumulation in the lungs of mononuclear phages and T lymphocyte cells that express this receptor.
